doc.title: Jimmy Wormworth interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002

title: Utica's remarkable musical talent
summary: He names Utica musicians such as John Simonelli, Torrie Zito and J.R. Monterose.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: One thing I’d like to add, Utica really outdid itself so to speak in the amount of talent that both resided there and came from there, just in the area of music. Whether it’s John Simonelli, who I think became the first chair hornist with the Philadelphia who played under Mason Jones. We played in all city high school band together. I could tell he was great then. He had an incredible sound on the French horn. He used to walk around rehearsal room before we started band rehearsal playing [scats] like that. I knew then, I was like thirteen or fourteen, I said wow, man, what a great sound that kid has. He was a little bit of a jokester but he became a world class French hornist. And well Torrie Zito, his accomplishments pretty much speak for themselves, all the arrangements he did for Tony Bennett of course, and something that maybe not too many people know now, he wrote the original Maxwell House jingle [scats].
And you’ve got the Mancusos, and a Montalbano. Lots of great people.
There are so many people, J.R. Monterose. My father, my uncle.
Uh I’m lucky to be part of a good wave.
